## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Ambavimānavatthu* ("Mango Mansion", Vv 79) is a verse text belonging to the *Vimānavatthu* collection [SuttaCentral]. In this narrative, a *deva* describes his past encounter with the arahant Sāriputta and explains the meritorious deeds he performed that led to his rebirth and happiness in a divine mansion [SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral records five translations of the text across five languages [SuttaCentral].
According to computational analysis by DharmaNexus, the text shares extensive material across 11 other Pali works, most notably with its commentary, the *Vimānavatthu-aṭṭhakathā*, which covers segments §1.1–12.4 [DharmaNexus]. It also exhibits significant internal formulaic overlap with numerous other poems in the *Vimānavatthu*, including the *Guttilavimānavatthu* (Vv 33), *Dvārapālavimānavatthu* (Vv 55), *Paṭhamasūcivimānavatthu* (Vv 58), and *Dutiyasūcivimānavatthu* (Vv 59) [DharmaNexus]. Outside Pali, DharmaNexus identifies low-scoring automated cross-language alignments with the Chinese *Saṃyuktāgama* (Taishō 99), though no established parallels are reported [DharmaNexus].
*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
